questions.q:
The Variance of the following probability distribution of X is
X$0$$1$$2$$3$
P(X)$q^3$$3q^2 p$$3qp^2$$p^3$
where $0 \lt p \lt 1, q = 1 - p$
questions.solution:
The given probability distribution represents a binomial distribution with parameters $n = 3$ and probability of success $p$, since $P(X = x) = ^{3}C_{x} p^x q^{3-x}$ for $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$.

For a binomial distribution, the variance is given by $npq$.

Substituting $n = 3$, the variance is $3pq$.

Alternatively, calculating the variance using expectations:

$E(X) = \sum x P(x) = 0(q^3) + 1(3q^2 p) + 2(3qp^2) + 3(p^3)$

$E(X) = 3p(q^2 + 2pq + p^2) = 3p(q+p)^2 = 3p$

$E(X^2) = \sum x^2 P(x) = 0(q^3) + 1(3q^2 p) + 4(3qp^2) + 9(p^3)$

$E(X^2) = 3p(q^2 + 4pq + 3p^2) = 3p((q+p)^2 + 2p(q+p)) = 3p(1 + 2p) = 3p + 6p^2$

$\text{Variance} = E(X^2) - (E(X))^2$

$\text{Variance} = 3p + 6p^2 - (3p)^2 = 3p - 3p^2 = 3p(1-p) = 3pq$

Answer: $3pq$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The centers for disease control have determined that when a person is given a vaccine, the probability that the person will develop immunity to a virus is $0.8$. If $8$ people are given this vaccine, then the probability that exactly $4$ will develop immunity is...
questions.solution:
Let $p$ be the probability of developing immunity, $p = 0.8$.

Let $q$ be the probability of not developing immunity, $q = 1 - p = 0.2$.

The number of trials is $n = 8$.

Using the binomial distribution formula, the probability of exactly $r$ successes is given by $P(X = r) = ^{n}C_{r} p^r q^{n-r}$.

For $r = 4$ successes:

$P(X = 4) = ^{8}C_{4} (0.8)^4 (0.2)^4$

Calculating $^{8}C_{4}$:

$^{8}C_{4} = \dfrac{8!}{4!(8-4)!} = \dfrac{8 \times 7 \times 6 \times 5}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 70$

Substituting this back into the probability expression:

$P(X = 4) = 70 \times (0.8)^4 \times (0.2)^4$

Since $(0.2)^4 = 0.0016$:

$70 \times (0.2)^4 = 70 \times 0.0016 = 0.112$

Therefore, $P(X = 4) = (0.112)(0.8)^4$.

Answer: $(0.112)(0.8)^4$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$ with usual notations, if $1 + \tan\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)\tan\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) = \dfrac{k}{s}$ (where $s$ is the semi-perimeter), then the value of $k$ is...
questions.solution:
Using the half-angle formulas for a triangle:

$\tan\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{(s-b)(s-c)}{s(s-a)}}$

$\tan\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{(s-a)(s-c)}{s(s-b)}}$

Multiplying these two expressions:

$\tan\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)\tan\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{(s-b)(s-c)}{s(s-a)} \dfrac{(s-a)(s-c)}{s(s-b)}} = \dfrac{s-c}{s}$

Substituting this into the given equation:

$1 + \tan\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)\tan\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) = 1 + \dfrac{s-c}{s} = \dfrac{2s - c}{s}$

Since $2s = a + b + c$, we have $2s - c = a + b$.

Therefore, $1 + \tan\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)\tan\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) = \dfrac{a + b}{s}$

Comparing this with $\dfrac{k}{s}$, we get $k = a + b$.

Answer: $a + b$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If a triangle $ABC$ has vertices $A(1,-6), B(2,-3)$ and $C(3,-2)$, then the coordinates of its orthocenter are....
questions.solution:
Let the vertices of the triangle be $A(1, -6)$, $B(2, -3)$, and $C(3, -2)$.

The slope of the side $BC$ is $m_{BC} = \dfrac{-2 - (-3)}{3 - 2} = 1$.
The altitude from $A$ to $BC$ is perpendicular to $BC$, so its slope is $-1$.
The equation of the altitude from $A(1, -6)$ is:
$y - (-6) = -1(x - 1)$
$x + y = -5$ ... (i)

The slope of the side $AC$ is $m_{AC} = \dfrac{-2 - (-6)}{3 - 1} = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2$.
The altitude from $B$ to $AC$ is perpendicular to $AC$, so its slope is $-\dfrac{1}{2}$.
The equation of the altitude from $B(2, -3)$ is:
$y - (-3) = -\dfrac{1}{2}(x - 2)$
$2y + 6 = -x + 2$
$x + 2y = -4$ ... (ii)

The orthocenter is the point of intersection of the altitudes. Solving equations (i) and (ii):
Subtracting (i) from (ii), we get:
$(x + 2y) - (x + y) = -4 - (-5)$
$y = 1$

Substituting $y = 1$ into equation (i):
$x + 1 = -5$
$x = -6$

The coordinates of the orthocenter are $(-6, 1)$.

Answer: $(-6, 1)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If a unit vector makes angles $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ with $\hat{i}$, $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with $\hat{j}$ and $\theta \in (0, \pi)$ with $\hat{k}$, then a value of $\theta$ is equal to...
questions.solution:
Let the unit vector be $\vec{a} = \cos\alpha \hat{i} + \cos\beta \hat{j} + \cos\gamma \hat{k}$.

Given $\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, $\beta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$, and $\gamma = \theta$.

Using the property of direction cosines, $\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1$.

Substituting the given values:

$\cos^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) + \cos^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) + \cos^2\theta = 1$

$\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \cos^2\theta = 1$

$\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{4} + \cos^2\theta = 1$

$\dfrac{3}{4} + \cos^2\theta = 1$

$\cos^2\theta = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$\cos\theta = \pm \dfrac{1}{2}$

Since $\theta \in (0, \pi)$, we get $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ or $\theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the plane containing the lines $\dfrac{x-1}{2} = \dfrac{y+1}{\lambda} = \dfrac{z}{2}$ and $\dfrac{x+1}{5} = \dfrac{y+1}{2} = \dfrac{z}{\lambda}$ is
questions.solution:
For the two lines to be coplanar, the shortest distance between them must be zero.

The first line passes through $A(1, -1, 0)$ with direction ratios $\vec{d}_1 = (2, \lambda, 2)$.

The second line passes through $B(-1, -1, 0)$ with direction ratios $\vec{d}_2 = (5, 2, \lambda)$.

The vector joining the points is $\vec{AB} = (-2, 0, 0)$.

The condition for coplanarity is $[\vec{AB}, \vec{d}_1, \vec{d}_2] = 0$:

$\begin{vmatrix} -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & \lambda & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & \lambda \end{vmatrix} = 0$

$-2(\lambda^2 - 4) = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = \pm 2$

Case 1: $\lambda = 2$

$\vec{d}_1 = (2, 2, 2)$ and $\vec{d}_2 = (5, 2, 2)$.

The normal vector to the plane is $\vec{n} = \vec{d}_1 \times \vec{d}_2 = (0, 6, -6)$, which is parallel to $(0, 1, -1)$.

The equation of the plane passing through $A(1, -1, 0)$ is:

$0(x - 1) + 1(y + 1) - 1(z - 0) = 0 \Rightarrow y - z + 1 = 0$

Case 2: $\lambda = -2$

$\vec{d}_1 = (2, -2, 2)$ and $\vec{d}_2 = (5, 2, -2)$.

The normal vector to the plane is $\vec{n} = \vec{d}_1 \times \vec{d}_2 = (0, 14, 14)$, which is parallel to $(0, 1, 1)$.

The equation of the plane passing through $A(1, -1, 0)$ is:

$0(x - 1) + 1(y + 1) + 1(z - 0) = 0 \Rightarrow y + z + 1 = 0$

Combining both cases, the equation of the plane is $y \pm z + 1 = 0$.

Answer: $y \pm z + 1 = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The direction cosines of a line which is perpendicular to the lines $\dfrac{x-7}{2} = \dfrac{y+17}{-3} = \dfrac{z-6}{1}$ and $\dfrac{x+5}{1} = \dfrac{y+3}{2} = \dfrac{z-6}{-2}$ are...
questions.solution:
Let the direction ratios of the required line be $a, b, c$.

Since the line is perpendicular to the given lines, its direction ratios satisfy:
$2a - 3b + c = 0$
$a + 2b - 2c = 0$

Solving by cross-multiplication:
$\dfrac{a}{(-3)(-2) - (1)(2)} = \dfrac{b}{(1)(1) - (2)(-2)} = \dfrac{c}{(2)(2) - (-3)(1)}$

$\dfrac{a}{6 - 2} = \dfrac{b}{1 + 4} = \dfrac{c}{4 + 3}$

$\dfrac{a}{4} = \dfrac{b}{5} = \dfrac{c}{7}$

The direction ratios are proportional to $4, 5, 7$.

The magnitude is $\sqrt{4^2 + 5^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{16 + 25 + 49} = \sqrt{90} = 3\sqrt{10}$.

Therefore, the direction cosines are $\dfrac{\pm 4}{3\sqrt{10}}, \dfrac{\pm 5}{3\sqrt{10}}, \dfrac{\pm 7}{3\sqrt{10}}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For the line $\dfrac{x+1}{1} = \dfrac{y-2}{2} = \dfrac{z+3}{3}$, identify the incorrect statement among the following.
options: It can be represented by equation $\dfrac{x+2}{1} = \dfrac{y}{2} = \dfrac{z+6}{3}$
It lies in the plane $x - 2y + z + 8 = 0$
It is perpendicular to the plane $x - 2y + z = 0$
questions.solution:
The given line is $\dfrac{x+1}{1} = \dfrac{y-2}{2} = \dfrac{z+3}{3} = \lambda$.

Any point on the line is of the form $(\lambda - 1, 2\lambda + 2, 3\lambda - 3)$.

For $\lambda = -1$, the point is $(-2, 0, -6)$. Since the direction ratios remain the same, the line can be represented as $\dfrac{x+2}{1} = \dfrac{y}{2} = \dfrac{z+6}{3}$. Thus, the first statement is correct.

Substituting the general point into the plane $x - 2y + z + 8 = 0$, we get $(\lambda - 1) - 2(2\lambda + 2) + (3\lambda - 3) + 8 = \lambda - 1 - 4\lambda - 4 + 3\lambda - 3 + 8 = 0$, which is true for all $\lambda$. Thus, the line lies in the plane, making the second statement correct.

For $\lambda = 1$, the point is $(0, 4, 0)$. Thus, the line passes through $(0, 4, 0)$, making the fourth statement correct.

The direction ratios of the line are $(1, 2, 3)$ and the normal to the plane $x - 2y + z = 0$ has direction ratios $(1, -2, 1)$. For the line to be perpendicular to the plane, their direction ratios must be proportional. Since $\dfrac{1}{1} \neq \dfrac{2}{-2} \neq \dfrac{3}{1}$, the line is not perpendicular to the plane. Thus, the third statement is incorrect.

Answer: It is perpendicular to the plane $x - 2y + z = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the lines $\dfrac{x-5}{5m+2} = \dfrac{2-y}{5} = \dfrac{1-z}{-1}$ and $x = \dfrac{2y+1}{4m} = \dfrac{1-z}{-3}$ are perpendicular to each other, then the value of m is ...
questions.solution:
Rewriting the equations of the given lines in standard form.

First line: $\dfrac{x-5}{5m+2} = \dfrac{y-2}{-5} = \dfrac{z-1}{1}$

Direction ratios of the first line are $a_1 = 5m+2$, $b_1 = -5$, $c_1 = 1$.

Second line: $\dfrac{x-0}{1} = \dfrac{y+\dfrac{1}{2}}{2m} = \dfrac{z-1}{3}$

Direction ratios of the second line are $a_2 = 1$, $b_2 = 2m$, $c_2 = 3$.

Since the lines are perpendicular, $a_1 a_2 + b_1 b_2 + c_1 c_2 = 0$.

$(5m+2)(1) + (-5)(2m) + (1)(3) = 0$

$5m + 2 - 10m + 3 = 0$

$-5m + 5 = 0$

$m = 1$

Answer: $1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\cos(p\theta) + \cos(q\theta) = 0$ and $p \neq q$, then the general value of $\theta$ (where n is any integer) is...
questions.solution:
Given $\cos(p\theta) + \cos(q\theta) = 0$

Using the formula $\cos C + \cos D = 2\cos\left(\dfrac{C+D}{2}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{C-D}{2}\right)$:

$2\cos\left(\dfrac{p+q}{2}\theta\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{p-q}{2}\theta\right) = 0$

This implies either $\cos\left(\dfrac{p+q}{2}\theta\right) = 0$ or $\cos\left(\dfrac{p-q}{2}\theta\right) = 0$

If $\cos\left(\dfrac{p+q}{2}\theta\right) = 0$, then $\dfrac{p+q}{2}\theta = (2n+1)\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, where $n$ is an integer.

$\theta = \dfrac{(2n+1)\pi}{p+q}$

If $\cos\left(\dfrac{p-q}{2}\theta\right) = 0$, then $\dfrac{p-q}{2}\theta = (2n+1)\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, where $n$ is an integer.

$\theta = \dfrac{(2n+1)\pi}{p-q}$

Combining both cases, the general value of $\theta$ is $\dfrac{(2n+1)\pi}{p \pm q}$

Answer: $\dfrac{(2n+1)\pi}{p \pm q}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $P = \tan 20^\circ$, then the value of $\dfrac{\tan 160^\circ - \tan 110^\circ}{1 + \tan 160^\circ \tan 110^\circ}$ in terms of $P$, is...
questions.solution:
We have $P = \tan 20^{\circ}$.

Expressing the terms in the given expression using $20^{\circ}$:

$\tan 160^{\circ} = \tan(180^{\circ} - 20^{\circ}) = -\tan 20^{\circ} = -P$

$\tan 110^{\circ} = \tan(90^{\circ} + 20^{\circ}) = -\cot 20^{\circ} = -\dfrac{1}{\tan 20^{\circ}} = -\dfrac{1}{P}$

Substituting these values into the given expression:

$\dfrac{\tan 160^{\circ} - \tan 110^{\circ}}{1 + \tan 160^{\circ} \tan 110^{\circ}} = \dfrac{-P - \left(-\dfrac{1}{P}\right)}{1 + (-P)\left(-\dfrac{1}{P}\right)}$

$= \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{P} - P}{1 + 1}$

$= \dfrac{\dfrac{1 - P^2}{P}}{2}$

$= \dfrac{1 - P^2}{2P}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1-P^2}{2P}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, with the usual notations, $\angle C = 90^\circ$, then $\sin(A - B)$ is equal to....
questions.solution:
In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C = 90^\circ$.

Using trigonometric ratios in a right-angled triangle:

$\sin A = \dfrac{a}{c}$

$\cos A = \dfrac{b}{c}$

$\sin B = \dfrac{b}{c}$

$\cos B = \dfrac{a}{c}$

Using the expansion formula for $\sin(A - B)$:

$\sin(A - B) = \sin A \cos B - \cos A \sin B$

Substituting the values:

$\sin(A - B) = \left(\dfrac{a}{c}\right)\left(\dfrac{a}{c}\right) - \left(\dfrac{b}{c}\right)\left(\dfrac{b}{c}\right)$

$\sin(A - B) = \dfrac{a^2 - b^2}{c^2}$

By Pythagoras theorem in $\triangle ABC$, $c^2 = a^2 + b^2$.

Substituting $c^2 = a^2 + b^2$:

$\sin(A - B) = \dfrac{a^2 - b^2}{a^2 + b^2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{a^2 - b^2}{a^2 + b^2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $(\bar{p} \wedge \bar{q})$ denote the angle between $\bar{p}$ and $\bar{q}$. If $\bar{a} + \bar{b} + \bar{c} = \bar{0}, |\bar{a}| = 7, |\bar{b}| = 5$ and $|\bar{c}| = 3$ then (take $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$)
questions.solution:
Given $\bar{a} + \bar{b} + \bar{c} = \bar{0}$, we can write $\bar{a} + \bar{c} = -\bar{b}$.

Squaring both sides, we get:

$|\bar{a}|^2 + |\bar{c}|^2 + 2|\bar{a}||\bar{c}|\cos(\bar{a} \wedge \bar{c}) = |\bar{b}|^2$

Substituting the given values $|\bar{a}| = 7$, $|\bar{b}| = 5$, and $|\bar{c}| = 3$:

$7^2 + 3^2 + 2(7)(3)\cos(\bar{a} \wedge \bar{c}) = 5^2$

$49 + 9 + 42\cos(\bar{a} \wedge \bar{c}) = 25$

$58 + 42\cos(\bar{a} \wedge \bar{c}) = 25$

$42\cos(\bar{a} \wedge \bar{c}) = -33$

$\cos(\bar{a} \wedge \bar{c}) = -\dfrac{33}{42} = -\dfrac{11}{14}$

Given $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$, we can rewrite the expression as:

$-\dfrac{11}{14} = -\dfrac{1}{4} \left(\dfrac{22}{7}\right) = -\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Therefore, $\cos(\bar{a} \wedge \bar{c}) = -\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

Answer: $\cos(\bar{a} \wedge \bar{c}) = -\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The vector $\bar{r}$ whose magnitude is $3\sqrt{2}$ units and which makes angles of $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ and $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ with the positive y- and z-axes respectively is....
questions.solution:
Let the direction cosines of the vector $\bar{r}$ be $l, m, n$.

Given that the vector makes angles $\beta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ and $\gamma = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ with the positive y- and z-axes respectively.

$m = \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$n = \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0$

Using the relation $l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1$:

$l^2 + \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 + 0 = 1$

$l^2 + \dfrac{1}{2} = 1 \Rightarrow l = \pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

The vector $\bar{r}$ is given by $|\bar{r}|(l\hat{i} + m\hat{j} + n\hat{k})$.

Substituting the values:

$\bar{r} = 3\sqrt{2} \left( \pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{i} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{j} + 0\hat{k} \right)$

$\bar{r} = \pm 3\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}$

Answer: $\pm 3\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If ABCDEF is a regular hexagon and $\overline{AB} + \overline{AC} + \overline{AD} + \overline{AE} + \overline{AF} = p\overline{AD} = q\overline{AO}$, where O is the center of the hexagon, then the values of $p$ and $q$ respectively are
questions.solution:
Let $O$ be the origin. The position vectors of the vertices $A, B, C, D, E, F$ are $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}, \vec{d}, \vec{e}, \vec{f}$ respectively.

Since $ABCDEF$ is a regular hexagon with center $O$, the position vectors of opposite vertices are negatives of each other. Thus, $\vec{d} = -\vec{a}$, $\vec{e} = -\vec{b}$, and $\vec{f} = -\vec{c}$.

The given sum of vectors is:

$\overrightarrow{AB} + \overrightarrow{AC} + \overrightarrow{AD} + \overrightarrow{AE} + \overrightarrow{AF}$

$= (\vec{b} - \vec{a}) + (\vec{c} - \vec{a}) + (\vec{d} - \vec{a}) + (\vec{e} - \vec{a}) + (\vec{f} - \vec{a})$

$= \vec{b} + \vec{c} + \vec{d} + \vec{e} + \vec{f} - 5\vec{a}$

Substituting $\vec{d} = -\vec{a}$, $\vec{e} = -\vec{b}$, and $\vec{f} = -\vec{c}$:

$= \vec{b} + \vec{c} - \vec{a} - \vec{b} - \vec{c} - 5\vec{a}$

$= -6\vec{a}$

The vector $\overrightarrow{AO}$ is given by $\vec{0} - \vec{a} = -\vec{a}$.

Therefore, the sum is $6(-\vec{a}) = 6\overrightarrow{AO}$.

Also, the vector $\overrightarrow{AD}$ is given by $\vec{d} - \vec{a} = -\vec{a} - \vec{a} = -2\vec{a} = 2\overrightarrow{AO}$.

Thus, the sum can be written as $3(-2\vec{a}) = 3\overrightarrow{AD}$.

Comparing this with $p\overrightarrow{AD} = q\overrightarrow{AO}$, we get $p = 3$ and $q = 6$.

Answer: $3, 6$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ are unit vectors and $\theta$ ($0 \lt  \theta \lt  \pi$) is the angle between them, then the value of $\dfrac{|\bar{a} + \bar{b}|}{|\bar{a} - \bar{b}|}$ is equal to...
questions.solution:
Given $|\bar{a}| = 1$ and $|\bar{b}| = 1$.

$|\bar{a} + \bar{b}|^2 = |\bar{a}|^2 + |\bar{b}|^2 + 2\bar{a}\cdot\bar{b} = 1 + 1 + 2\cos\theta = 2(1 + \cos\theta) = 4\cos^2\dfrac{\theta}{2}$

$|\bar{a} - \bar{b}|^2 = |\bar{a}|^2 + |\bar{b}|^2 - 2\bar{a}\cdot\bar{b} = 1 + 1 - 2\cos\theta = 2(1 - \cos\theta) = 4\sin^2\dfrac{\theta}{2}$

Taking the square root, since $0 \lt \theta \lt \pi$, we have $\cos\dfrac{\theta}{2} \gt 0$ and $\sin\dfrac{\theta}{2} \gt 0$:

$|\bar{a} + \bar{b}| = 2\cos\dfrac{\theta}{2}$

$|\bar{a} - \bar{b}| = 2\sin\dfrac{\theta}{2}$

$\dfrac{|\bar{a} + \bar{b}|}{|\bar{a} - \bar{b}|} = \dfrac{2\cos\dfrac{\theta}{2}}{2\sin\dfrac{\theta}{2}} = \cot\dfrac{\theta}{2}$

Answer: $\cot\dfrac{\theta}{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A coil has inductive reactance $3$ H. The ratio of its reactance when it is first connected to an a.c. source and then to d.c. source is
questions.solution:
The inductive reactance of a coil is given by $X_L = \omega L = 2\pi f L$, where $f$ is the frequency of the source.

For an a.c. source, the frequency $f \gt 0$, so the inductive reactance $X_{L(ac)}$ has a finite non-zero value.

For a d.c. source, the frequency $f = 0$, so the inductive reactance $X_{L(dc)} = 0$.

The ratio of the reactance when connected to an a.c. source to that when connected to a d.c. source is:

$\text{Ratio} = \dfrac{X_{L(ac)}}{X_{L(dc)}} = \dfrac{\omega L}{0} = \infty$

Thus, the ratio is infinite.

Answer: infinite

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Determine the frequency for which a $10\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitor has a reactance of $2 \times 10^{-3}\,\Omega$.
questions.solution:
The capacitive reactance is given by the formula:

$X_C = \dfrac{1}{2\pi f C}$

Rearranging for frequency $f$:

$f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi X_C C}$

Substituting the given values $X_C = 2 \times 10^{-3} \, \Omega$ and $C = 10 \, \mu\text{F} = 10 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F}$:

$f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi \times (2 \times 10^{-3}) \times (10 \times 10^{-6})}$

$f = \dfrac{1}{4\pi \times 10^{-8}}$

$f = \dfrac{10^8}{4\pi}$

$f = \dfrac{100 \times 10^6}{4\pi}$

$f = \dfrac{25}{\pi} \times 10^6 \, \text{Hz}$

$f = \dfrac{25}{\pi} \, \text{MHz}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A series LCR circuit is connected to an a.c. source of $220$ V, $50$ Hz. The circuit contains a resistance $R = 80\,\Omega$, an inductor of inductive reactance $70\,\Omega$ and capacitor of capacitive reactance $130\,\Omega$. The power factor of the circuit is $\dfrac{x}{10}$. The value of x is
questions.solution:
The impedance of the series LCR circuit is given by

$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_C - X_L)^2}$

Substituting the given values:

$Z = \sqrt{80^2 + (130 - 70)^2}$

$Z = \sqrt{80^2 + 60^2}$

$Z = \sqrt{6400 + 3600} = \sqrt{10000} = 100\,\Omega$

The power factor of the circuit is

$\cos \phi = \dfrac{R}{Z}$

$\cos \phi = \dfrac{80}{100} = \dfrac{8}{10}$

Comparing this with $\dfrac{x}{10}$, we get $x = 8$.

Answer: $8$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If 'E' and 'L' denote the magnitude of total energy and angular momentum of revolving electron in $n^{th}$ Bohr orbit then
questions.solution:
The magnitude of total energy of an electron in the $n^{th}$ Bohr orbit is given by $E \propto \dfrac{1}{n^2}$.

The angular momentum of the electron in the $n^{th}$ Bohr orbit is given by $L = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$.

This implies $L \propto n$.

Substituting $n \propto L$ in the expression for energy, we get $E \propto \dfrac{1}{L^2}$.

Thus, $E \propto L^{-2}$.

Answer: $E \propto L^{-2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When the electron orbiting in hydrogen atom in its ground state moves to the third excited state, the de-Broglie wavelength associated with it
questions.solution:
According to Bohr's model, the velocity of an electron in the $n$-th orbit is given by $v \propto \dfrac{1}{n}$.

The de-Broglie wavelength of the electron is $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}$.

Substituting the proportionality of velocity, we get $\lambda \propto n$.

The ground state corresponds to $n = 1$ and the third excited state corresponds to $n = 4$.

Since $n$ increases from $1$ to $4$, the de-Broglie wavelength of the electron will increase.

Answer: will increase

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Four capacitors are connected to a battery as shown in figure. The ratio of charges on capacitors $C_2$ and $C_4$ is
questions.solution:
From the given circuit diagram, capacitors $C_1$, $C_2$, and $C_3$ are connected in series. This series combination is connected in parallel with capacitor $C_4$ across the battery of voltage $V$.

The equivalent capacitance $C_s$ of the series branch containing $C_1$, $C_2$, and $C_3$ is given by:

$\dfrac{1}{C_s} = \dfrac{1}{C_1} + \dfrac{1}{C_2} + \dfrac{1}{C_3}$

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{1}{C_s} = \dfrac{1}{1C} + \dfrac{1}{2C} + \dfrac{1}{3C} = \dfrac{6 + 3 + 2}{6C} = \dfrac{11}{6C}$

$C_s = \dfrac{6C}{11}$

Since $C_1$, $C_2$, and $C_3$ are in series, the charge on each of them is the same and is equal to the total charge on this series branch. The voltage across this branch is $V$.

Charge on $C_2$, $Q_2 = C_s \times V = \dfrac{6CV}{11}$

Capacitor $C_4$ is connected directly across the battery, so the voltage across it is also $V$.

Charge on $C_4$, $Q_4 = C_4 \times V = 4CV$

The ratio of charges on $C_2$ and $C_4$ is:

$\dfrac{Q_2}{Q_4} = \dfrac{\dfrac{6CV}{11}}{4CV} = \dfrac{6}{11 \times 4} = \dfrac{6}{44} = \dfrac{3}{22}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{22}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The function of a dielectric in a capacitor is to
options: reduce the plate area of the capacitor.
reduce the effective potential on plates.
increase the effective potential on plates.
questions.solution:
When a dielectric material is introduced between the plates of a capacitor, it gets polarized due to the external electric field. This polarization creates an induced electric field inside the dielectric which opposes the external electric field.

As a result, the net electric field between the plates decreases. Since the potential difference is given by $V = E \times d$, the effective potential difference between the plates also decreases for a given charge.

This reduction in potential difference leads to an increase in the capacitance of the capacitor, as $C = \dfrac{Q}{V}$. Therefore, the function of a dielectric is to reduce the effective potential on the plates.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The potential difference that must be applied across the parallel and series combination of three identical capacitors such that the energy stored in them becomes the same. The ratio of potential difference in parallel to series combination is
questions.solution:
Let the capacitance of each identical capacitor be $C$.

For the parallel combination, the equivalent capacitance is $C_p = 3C$.

The energy stored in the parallel combination when a potential difference $V_p$ is applied is $U_p = \dfrac{1}{2}C_p V_p^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}(3C)V_p^2$.

For the series combination, the equivalent capacitance is $C_s = \dfrac{C}{3}$.

The energy stored in the series combination when a potential difference $V_s$ is applied is $U_s = \dfrac{1}{2}C_s V_s^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{C}{3}\right)V_s^2$.

Given that the energy stored in both combinations is the same, $U_p = U_s$.

$\dfrac{1}{2}(3C)V_p^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{C}{3}\right)V_s^2$

$3V_p^2 = \dfrac{V_s^2}{3}$

$\dfrac{V_p^2}{V_s^2} = \dfrac{1}{9}$

$\dfrac{V_p}{V_s} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

The ratio of potential difference in parallel to series combination is $1:3$.

Answer: $1:3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.q: Two masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ moving with velocities $V_1$ and $V_2$ in opposite directions collide elastically and after collision $m_1$ and $m_2$ move with velocities $V_2$ and $V_1$ respectively. The ratio $\dfrac{m_2}{m_1}$ is
questions.solution:
By the principle of conservation of linear momentum:

$m_1 \vec{V}_1 + m_2 \vec{V}_2 = m_1 \vec{V}_1' + m_2 \vec{V}_2'$

Given that the final velocities are $\vec{V}_1' = \vec{V}_2$ and $\vec{V}_2' = \vec{V}_1$, we substitute these into the momentum equation:

$m_1 \vec{V}_1 + m_2 \vec{V}_2 = m_1 \vec{V}_2 + m_2 \vec{V}_1$

Rearranging the terms yields:

$m_1 (\vec{V}_1 - \vec{V}_2) = m_2 (\vec{V}_1 - \vec{V}_2)$

Since the masses are moving in opposite directions, $\vec{V}_1 \neq \vec{V}_2$, which implies $\vec{V}_1 - \vec{V}_2 \neq 0$.

Dividing both sides by $(\vec{V}_1 - \vec{V}_2)$ gives:

$m_1 = m_2$

Therefore, the ratio $\dfrac{m_2}{m_1} = 1.0$.

Note: In a perfectly elastic collision in one dimension, the velocities of the two bodies are exchanged if and only if their masses are equal.

Answer: $1.0$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If a galvanometer is shunted by $\left(\dfrac{1}{n-1}\right)^{th}$ of the value of its resistance, then the fraction of the total current passing through the galvanometer is
questions.solution:
Let the resistance of the galvanometer be $G$ and the total current in the circuit be $I$.

The shunt resistance is given as $S = \dfrac{G}{n-1}$.

Since the galvanometer and the shunt are connected in parallel, the potential difference across them is equal:

$I_g G = (I - I_g) S$

Substituting the value of $S$:

$I_g G = (I - I_g) \dfrac{G}{n-1}$

$I_g (n-1) = I - I_g$

$n I_g - I_g + I_g = I$

$n I_g = I$

$\dfrac{I_g}{I} = \dfrac{1}{n}$

The fraction of the total current passing through the galvanometer is \dfrac{1}{n}.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{n}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a resistance of $200\,\Omega$ is connected in series with a galvanometer of resistance G, its range is V. To triple its range, a resistance of $2000\,\Omega$ is connected in series. The value of G is
questions.solution:
Let $I_g$ be the current for full scale deflection of the galvanometer.

When a resistance of $200\,\Omega$ is connected in series, the range is $V$.

$V = I_g(G + 200)$

When a resistance of $2000\,\Omega$ is connected in series, the range becomes $3V$.

$3V = I_g(G + 2000)$

Dividing the second equation by the first equation:

$\dfrac{3V}{V} = \dfrac{I_g(G + 2000)}{I_g(G + 200)}$

$3 = \dfrac{G + 2000}{G + 200}$

$3G + 600 = G + 2000$

$2G = 1400$

$G = 700\,\Omega$

Answer: $700\,\Omega$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Light of wavelength '$\lambda$' which is less than threshold wavelength is incident on a photosensitive material. If incident wavelength is decreased so that emitted photoelectrons are moving with some velocity then stopping potential
questions.solution:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is given by

$K_{\max} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \Phi$

where $\lambda$ is the incident wavelength and $\Phi$ is the work function of the material.

The stopping potential $V_s$ is related to the maximum kinetic energy by

$eV_s = K_{\max} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \Phi$

When the incident wavelength $\lambda$ is decreased, the term $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$ increases. Since the work function $\Phi$ remains constant for a given material, the maximum kinetic energy $K_{\max}$ of the photoelectrons increases.

Consequently, the stopping potential $V_s$ also increases.

Answer: increases

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A bar magnet falls from a height 'h' through a metal pipe, its acceleration after coming out of pipe is
questions.solution:
When the bar magnet falls through the metal pipe, the changing magnetic flux induces eddy currents in the pipe.

According to Lenz's law, these eddy currents oppose the motion of the magnet, making its acceleration less than $g$ ($9.8 \text{ m/s}^2$) while inside the pipe.

Once the magnet comes out of the pipe, there is no induced current to oppose its motion.

The only force acting on the magnet is gravity.

Therefore, its acceleration after coming out of the pipe is equal to the acceleration due to gravity, which is $9.8 \text{ m/s}^2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The coefficient of mutual induction is $3$H and induced e.m.f. across secondary is $4$ kV. Current in primary is reduced from $7$A to $2$A. The time required for the change of current is
questions.solution:
The magnitude of induced e.m.f. in the secondary coil is given by

$|e| = M \left| \dfrac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \right|$

Substituting the given values:

$4000 = 3 \times \left| \dfrac{2 - 7}{\Delta t} \right|$

$4000 = \dfrac{15}{\Delta t}$

$\Delta t = \dfrac{15}{4000} = 3.75 \times 10^{-3}$ s

Answer: $3.75 \times 10^{-3}$ s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A coil of 'n' turns and resistance $R\,\Omega$ is connected in series with a resistance $R/4$. The combination is moved for time 't' second through flux $\Phi_1$ to $\Phi_2$. The induced current in the circuit is
questions.solution:
The total resistance of the circuit is given by the sum of the coil's resistance and the series resistance:

$R_{eq} = R + \dfrac{R}{4} = \dfrac{5R}{4}$

According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the average induced emf in a coil of $n$ turns is:

$E = -n \dfrac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = -n \dfrac{\Phi_2 - \Phi_1}{t} = \dfrac{n(\Phi_1 - \Phi_2)}{t}$

The induced current in the circuit is the ratio of the induced emf to the total resistance:

$I = \dfrac{E}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{n(\Phi_1 - \Phi_2)}{t}}{\dfrac{5R}{4}} = \dfrac{4n(\Phi_1 - \Phi_2)}{5Rt}$

Using $T$ for time as given in the options, the induced current is $\dfrac{4n(\Phi_1 - \Phi_2)}{5RT}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The number of lines of force originating from a point charge of $2 \times 8.85 \times 10^{-9}$ C in a medium of dielectric constant $10$ is ($\epsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}$ SI unit)
questions.solution:
0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}$ SI unit

Substituting the values:
$\Phi = \dfrac{2 \times 8.85 \times 10^{-9}}{10 \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12}}$

$\Phi = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{-9}}{10^{-11}}$

$\Phi = 200$

Answer: $200$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What should be the angular velocity of earth due to rotation about its own axis so that the weight at equator becomes $\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^{th}$ of initial value? ($g =$ acceleration due to gravity, R = radius of earth)
questions.solution:
The effective acceleration due to gravity at the equator due to the rotation of the Earth is given by:

$g' = g - \omega^2 R$

The weight of a body at the equator is:

$W' = mg' = m(g - \omega^2 R)$

According to the given condition, the new weight becomes $\dfrac{3}{5}$ of the initial weight ($mg$).

$m(g - \omega^2 R) = \dfrac{3}{5} mg$

$g - \omega^2 R = \dfrac{3}{5} g$

$\omega^2 R = g - \dfrac{3}{5} g$

$\omega^2 R = \dfrac{2}{5} g$

$\omega^2 = \dfrac{2g}{5R}$

$\omega = \left(\dfrac{2g}{5R}\right)^{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{2g}{5R}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The average force applied on the walls of a closed container depends on temperature (T) as (T is the temperature of an ideal gas)
questions.solution:
For an ideal gas in a closed container, the volume $V$ and the number of moles $n$ are constant.

Using the ideal gas equation, $PV = nRT$.

Since $V$, $n$, and $R$ are constants, the pressure $P$ is directly proportional to the absolute temperature $T$, i.e., $P \propto T$.

The average force $F$ exerted by the gas on the walls of the container is given by $F = P \times A$, where $A$ is the surface area of the walls.

Since the container is closed and rigid, the area $A$ is constant.

Therefore, $F \propto P \propto T$.

The average force depends on temperature as $T^1$.

Answer: $T^1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Lorentz magnetic force is acting on a particle of charge $q$ moving with velocity $\vec{V}$ in magnetic field $\vec{B}$. The work done by this force on the charged particle is
questions.solution:
The Lorentz magnetic force on a charged particle is given by $\vec{F} = q(\vec{V} \times \vec{B})$.

The power delivered by this force is $P = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{V} = q(\vec{V} \times \vec{B}) \cdot \vec{V}$.

Since the cross product $\vec{V} \times \vec{B}$ is always perpendicular to the velocity vector $\vec{V}$, their dot product is zero.

Thus, $P = 0$.

The work done by the magnetic force is $W = \int P dt = 0$.

Therefore, the work done by the Lorentz magnetic force on the charged particle is zero.

Answer: zero

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular coil of 'N' turns and diameter 'd' carries current 'I'. It is unwound and rewound to make another coil of diameter '2d', current 'I' remaining the Same. The ratio of magnetic moments of the new coil to the original coil is
questions.solution:
Length of the wire remains constant.

$L = N \times \pi d = N' \times \pi (2d)$

$N' = \dfrac{N}{2}$

Magnetic moment of the original coil is $M_1 = N I A_1 = N I \left( \dfrac{\pi d^2}{4} \right)$

Magnetic moment of the new coil is $M_2 = N' I A_2 = \left( \dfrac{N}{2} \right) I \left( \dfrac{\pi (2d)^2}{4} \right) = \dfrac{N}{2} I (\pi d^2)$

Ratio of magnetic moments is $\dfrac{M_2}{M_1} = \dfrac{\dfrac{N}{2} I \pi d^2}{N I \dfrac{\pi d^2}{4}} = \dfrac{1/2}{1/4} = 2$

The ratio is $2:1$.

Answer: $2:1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The product of magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$) and absolute temperature (T) is constant for a
options: paramagnetic as well as ferromagnetic substance.
questions.solution:
According to Curie's law, the magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$) of a paramagnetic substance is inversely proportional to its absolute temperature ($T$).

$\chi \propto \dfrac{1}{T}$

$\chi = \dfrac{C}{T}$

$\chi T = C$

where $C$ is Curie's constant. Thus, the product of magnetic susceptibility and absolute temperature is constant for a paramagnetic substance.

For diamagnetic substances, susceptibility is independent of temperature. For ferromagnetic substances, susceptibility follows the Curie-Weiss law ($\chi = \dfrac{C}{T - T_c}$) above the Curie temperature.

Answer: paramagnetic substance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A vector $\vec{A}$ when added to the sum of the vectors $(\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})$ and $(-2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k})$ gives a unit vector along Y axis. The magnitude of vector $\vec{A}$ is
questions.solution:
Let the given vectors be $\vec{V}_1 = \hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{V}_2 = -2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$.

The sum of these vectors is $\vec{V}_1 + \vec{V}_2 = -\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}$.

According to the given condition, $\vec{A} + (\vec{V}_1 + \vec{V}_2) = \hat{j}$.

Substituting the sum, we get $\vec{A} + (-\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = \hat{j}$.

$\vec{A} = \hat{j} - (-\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}$.

The magnitude of vector $\vec{A}$ is $|\vec{A}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 2^2 + (-1)^2} = \sqrt{6}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{6}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The length of rod is measured by meter scale having least count $0.1$ cm and diameter is measured by vernier callipers having least count $0.01$ cm. Length of rod is $5.0$ cm and radius $2.0$ cm. The percentage error in the calculated value of the volume is
questions.solution:
The volume of the cylindrical rod is given by $V = \dfrac{\pi D^2 L}{4}$, where $D$ is the diameter and $L$ is the length.

The percentage error in the volume is given by:
$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100 = \left( 2\dfrac{\Delta D}{D} + \dfrac{\Delta L}{L} \right) \times 100$

Given that the diameter is measured by vernier callipers, the measured quantity is $D$.
Radius $r = 2.0$ cm \Rightarrow Diameter $D = 4.0$ cm
Least count of vernier callipers, $\Delta D = 0.01$ cm
Length $L = 5.0$ cm
Least count of meter scale, $\Delta L = 0.1$ cm

Substituting the values into the percentage error formula:
$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100 = \left( 2 \times \dfrac{0.01}{4.0} + \dfrac{0.1}{5.0} \right) \times 100$

$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100 = \left( \dfrac{0.02}{4.0} + \dfrac{0.1}{5.0} \right) \times 100$

$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100 = \left( \dfrac{1}{200} + \dfrac{1}{50} \right) \times 100$

$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100 = \dfrac{100}{200} + \dfrac{100}{50} = 0.5 + 2 = 2.5\%$

Answer: $2.5\%$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The excess pressure inside the first soap bubble of radius $R_1$ is three times that inside the second soap bubble of radius $R_2$. The ratio of volumes of the first bubble to second bubble is
questions.solution:
The excess pressure inside a soap bubble of radius $R$ is given by $\Delta P = \dfrac{4T}{R}$.

Given that $\Delta P_1 = 3\Delta P_2$.

$\dfrac{4T}{R_1} = 3 \left(\dfrac{4T}{R_2}\right)$

$\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

The volume of a spherical bubble is $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3$.

The ratio of their volumes is $\dfrac{V_1}{V_2} = \left(\dfrac{R_1}{R_2}\right)^3 = \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^3 = \dfrac{1}{27}$.

Thus, the ratio of volumes is $1:27$.

Answer: $1:27$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A soap bubble of radius R is blown. After heating the solution, a second bubble of radius 2R is blown. The work required to blow the second bubble in comparison to that required for the first bubble is
questions.solution:
The work done in blowing a soap bubble of radius $R$ is given by $W = 2 \times 4\pi R^2 \times T = 8\pi R^2 T$, where $T$ is the surface tension of the soap solution.

For the first bubble of radius $R$, the work done is $W_1 = 8\pi R^2 T_1$.

For the second bubble of radius $2R$, the work done is $W_2 = 8\pi (2R)^2 T_2 = 32\pi R^2 T_2$.

The ratio of the work done is $\dfrac{W_2}{W_1} = \dfrac{32\pi R^2 T_2}{8\pi R^2 T_1} = 4 \dfrac{T_2}{T_1}$.

When the solution is heated, its temperature increases. The surface tension of a liquid decreases with an increase in temperature, so $T_2 \lt T_1$.

Therefore, $\dfrac{W_2}{W_1} \lt 4$, which means the work required to blow the second bubble is slightly less than $4$ times the work required for the first bubble.

Answer: slightly less than $4$ times

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Water rises to a height $3$ cm in a capillary tube. If cross-sectional area of capillary tube is reduced to $1/3^{rd}$ of its initial area then water will rise to a height of
questions.solution:
The height of water in a capillary tube is given by $h = \dfrac{2T \cos \theta}{\rho g r}$

This implies $h \propto \dfrac{1}{r}$

Given that the cross-sectional area is reduced to $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of its initial value:

$A_2 = \dfrac{A_1}{3}$

$\pi r_2^2 = \dfrac{\pi r_1^2}{3}$

$r_2 = \dfrac{r_1}{\sqrt{3}}$

Using the relation $h_1 r_1 = h_2 r_2$:

$h_2 = h_1 \dfrac{r_1}{r_2}$

$h_2 = 3 \times \sqrt{3} = 3\sqrt{3}$ cm

Answer: $3\sqrt{3}$ cm

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stone falls from the top of a tower of height $100$ m and at the same time another stone is projected vertically upwards from the ground with a velocity $25$ m/s. The two stones meet after
questions.solution:
Let the two stones meet after time $t$.

For the stone falling from the top of the tower:
Displacement downwards, $h_1 = \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2$

For the stone projected upwards from the ground:
Displacement upwards, $h_2 = 25t - \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2$

When the two stones meet, the sum of their displacements is equal to the height of the tower.
$h_1 + h_2 = 100$

$\dfrac{1}{2}gt^2 + 25t - \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2 = 100$

$25t = 100$

$t = 4$ s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle performing U.C.M. of radius $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ m makes 'x' revolutions in time t. Its tangential velocity is
questions.solution:
The radius of the circular path is $r = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ m.

The particle makes $x$ revolutions in time $t$, so its frequency is $n = \dfrac{x}{t}$.

The angular velocity is given by $\omega = 2\pi n = \dfrac{2\pi x}{t}$.

The tangential velocity is $v = r\omega$.

Substituting the values, we get $v = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \left(\dfrac{2\pi x}{t}\right) = \dfrac{\pi^2 x}{t}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi^2 x}{t}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two different radioactive elements with half lives $T_1$ and $T_2$ have undecayed atoms $N_1$ and $N_2$ respectively, present at a given instant. The ratio of their activities at this instant is
questions.solution:
Activity of a radioactive element is given by $A = \lambda N$

The decay constant $\lambda$ is related to half-life $T$ as $\lambda = \dfrac{\ln 2}{T}$

For the first element, activity $A_1 = \dfrac{\ln 2}{T_1} N_1$

For the second element, activity $A_2 = \dfrac{\ln 2}{T_2} N_2$

The ratio of their activities is $\dfrac{A_1}{A_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\ln 2}{T_1} N_1}{\dfrac{\ln 2}{T_2} N_2} = \dfrac{N_1 T_2}{N_2 T_1}$

Answer: $\dfrac{N_1 T_2}{N_2 T_1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A small sphere oscillates simple harmonically in a watch glass whose radius of curvature is $1.6$ m. The period of Oscillation of the sphere is (Acceleration due to gravity $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
The oscillation of a small sphere in a watch glass of radius of curvature $R$ is equivalent to a simple pendulum of effective length $R$.

The time period of oscillation is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{R}{g}}$.

Given $R = 1.6$ m and $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$.

Substituting the values:

$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{1.6}{10}}$

$T = 2\pi \sqrt{0.16}$

$T = 2\pi \times 0.4 = 0.8\pi$ s.

Answer: $0.8\pi$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle starts from mean position and performs S.H.M. with period $6$ second. At what time its kinetic energy is $50\%$ of total energy? ($\cos 45^\circ = 1/\sqrt{2}$)
questions.solution:
The displacement of a particle starting from the mean position is given by $x = A \sin(\omega t)$.

The velocity of the particle is $v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = A \omega \cos(\omega t)$.

The kinetic energy is $K = \dfrac{1}{2} m v^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} m A^2 \omega^2 \cos^2(\omega t)$.

The total energy of the particle in S.H.M. is $E = \dfrac{1}{2} m A^2 \omega^2$.

Given that the kinetic energy is $50\%$ of the total energy:

$K = \dfrac{E}{2}$

$\dfrac{1}{2} m A^2 \omega^2 \cos^2(\omega t) = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{1}{2} m A^2 \omega^2 \right)$

$\cos^2(\omega t) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\cos(\omega t) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\omega t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Substituting $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$:

$\dfrac{2\pi}{T} t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$t = \dfrac{T}{8}$

Given $T = 6$ s:

$t = \dfrac{6}{8} = 0.75$ s.

Answer: $0.75$ s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle executes linear S.H.M. with amplitude $4$ cm. The magnitude of velocity and acceleration is equal when it is at $3$ cm from mean position. Time period is
questions.solution:
Given amplitude $A = 4$ cm and displacement $x = 3$ cm.

The magnitude of velocity of a particle in S.H.M. is given by $v = \omega \sqrt{A^2 - x^2}$.

The magnitude of acceleration is given by $a = \omega^2 x$.

According to the given condition, $v = a$ at $x = 3$ cm.

$\omega \sqrt{A^2 - x^2} = \omega^2 x$

$\sqrt{4^2 - 3^2} = \omega (3)$

$\sqrt{16 - 9} = 3\omega$

$\sqrt{7} = 3\omega$

$\omega = \dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{3}$ rad/s

The time period $T$ is given by $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$.

$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{3}} = \dfrac{6\pi}{\sqrt{7}}$ s

Answer: $\dfrac{6\pi}{\sqrt{7}}$ s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ray of light travels from air to water to glass and again from glass to air. Refractive index of water with respect to air is 'x', glass with respect to water is 'y' and air with respect to glass is 'z'. Which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
Let the absolute refractive indices of air, water, and glass be $n_a$, $n_w$, and $n_g$ respectively.

Refractive index of water with respect to air is $x = \dfrac{n_w}{n_a}$

Refractive index of glass with respect to water is $y = \dfrac{n_g}{n_w}$

Refractive index of air with respect to glass is $z = \dfrac{n_a}{n_g}$

Multiplying the three equations, we get:

$x y z = \dfrac{n_w}{n_a} \times \dfrac{n_g}{n_w} \times \dfrac{n_a}{n_g}$

$x y z = 1$

Answer: $xyz = 1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An equiconvex lens of focal length F is cut in to two equal parts along the vertical axis. The focal length of each part will be
questions.solution:
Using the lens maker's formula for the initial equiconvex lens:

$\dfrac{1}{F} = (\mu - 1) \left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{-R}\right) = \dfrac{2(\mu - 1)}{R}$

When the lens is cut into two equal parts along the vertical axis, each part becomes a plano-convex lens with radii of curvature $R$ and $\infty$.

The focal length $F'$ of each part is given by:

$\dfrac{1}{F'} = (\mu - 1) \left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right) = \dfrac{\mu - 1}{R}$

Comparing the two equations:

$\dfrac{1}{F'} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{2(\mu - 1)}{R} \right) = \dfrac{1}{2F}$

$F' = 2F$

Answer: $2F$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the earth suddenly contracts to $\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^{rd}$ of its present size without change in its mass, the ratio kinetic energy of the earth after and before contraction will be (Earth is assumed to be a rotating sphere about itself)
questions.solution:
By conservation of angular momentum, $L_1 = L_2$.

The rotational kinetic energy is given by $K = \dfrac{L^2}{2I}$.

The ratio of final to initial kinetic energy is $\dfrac{K_2}{K_1} = \dfrac{I_1}{I_2}$.

The moment of inertia of a solid sphere is $I = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2$.

Given $R_2 = \dfrac{R_1}{3}$, we have $I_2 = \dfrac{2}{5}M\left(\dfrac{R_1}{3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{I_1}{9}$.

Therefore, $\dfrac{K_2}{K_1} = \dfrac{I_1}{\dfrac{I_1}{9}} = 9$.

Answer: $9$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The power (P) is supplied to rotating body having moment of inertia 'I' and angular acceleration '$\alpha$'. Its instantaneous angular velocity is
questions.solution:
Power $P$ supplied to a rotating body is given by the product of torque $\tau$ and angular velocity $\omega$.

$P = \tau \omega$

The torque $\tau$ acting on the body is related to its moment of inertia $I$ and angular acceleration $\alpha$ by the relation:

$\tau = I \alpha$

Substituting the value of $\tau$ in the power equation:

$P = (I \alpha) \omega$

Rearranging for instantaneous angular velocity $\omega$:

$\omega = \dfrac{P}{I \alpha}$

Answer: $\dfrac{P}{I\alpha}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If p-n junction diode is forward biased then
questions.solution:
When a p-n junction diode is forward biased, the positive terminal of the external voltage source is connected to the p-side and the negative terminal to the n-side.

The applied forward voltage opposes the built-in potential barrier, reducing the effective barrier voltage.

This external electric field pushes the majority charge carriers (holes in the p-region and electrons in the n-region) towards the junction.

As the carriers move towards the junction, they neutralize some of the immobile ions, which causes the width of the depletion layer to decrease.

This allows majority carriers to cross the junction easily, facilitating electric conduction.

Answer: width of depletion layer decreases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a p-n junction diode, breakdown voltage occurs when
questions.solution:
In a p-n junction diode, when the reverse bias voltage is increased, the width of the depletion region and the electric field across it increase.

At a sufficiently high reverse bias voltage, the electric field becomes strong enough to break covalent bonds (Zener breakdown) or accelerate minority carriers to cause impact ionization (avalanche breakdown).

This leads to a sudden and sharp increase in the reverse current, which is known as the breakdown voltage. Therefore, breakdown occurs when the reverse bias is increased.

Answer: reverse-bias is increased

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Photodiode is a device
options: in which photocurrent is dependent on reverse bias.
in which photocurrent is independent of incident radiation.
which is always operated in forward bias.
which is always operated in reverse bias.
questions.solution:
A photodiode is a p-n junction fabricated from a photosensitive semiconductor and provided with a transparent window to allow light to fall on its junction.

It is always operated under reverse bias. When the photodiode is illuminated with light (photons) with energy $h\nu$ greater than the energy gap $E_g$ of the semiconductor, electron-hole pairs are generated due to the absorption of photons.

Operating it in reverse bias makes it easier to observe changes in current with light intensity, because the fractional change in minority carrier current is much larger than the fractional change in majority carrier current (which would dominate in forward bias).

The photocurrent is directly proportional to the intensity of incident radiation and is largely independent of the reverse bias voltage.

Answer: which is always operated in reverse bias.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: About black body radiation, which one of the following is a WRONG statement?
options: For all wavelengths, power radiated is same
For shorter wavelengths, radiated power is more
for longer wavelengths, radiated power is less
All wavelengths are emitted by the black body
questions.solution:
According to the spectral distribution of black body radiation (Planck's law), a black body emits radiation of all possible wavelengths, but the energy is not uniformly distributed among them.

The spectral emissive power ($E_{\lambda}$) first increases with an increase in wavelength, reaches a maximum value at a specific wavelength ($\lambda_{m}$), and then decreases for longer wavelengths.

Therefore, the statement "For all wavelengths, power radiated is same" is completely incorrect.

Answer: For all wavelengths, power radiated is same

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A black disc has a radius 'R' and wavelength corresponding to the maximum intensity is '$\lambda$'. The emissive power (E) for the different radii and maximum wavelengths is directly proportional to
questions.solution:
The total emissive power of a black body is given by the Stefan-Boltzmann law:

$E = A \sigma T^4$

For a disc of radius $R$, the surface area $A \propto R^2$. Therefore, the emissive power is proportional to:

$E \propto R^2 T^4$

According to Wien's displacement law, the wavelength corresponding to maximum intensity $\lambda$ is related to the absolute temperature $T$ as:

$\lambda T = b$

$T \propto \lambda^{-1}$

Substituting this into the proportionality for $E$, we get:

$E \propto R^2 (\lambda^{-1})^4$

$E \propto R^2 \lambda^{-4}$

Answer: $R^2, \lambda^{-4}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ordinary body cools from $4\theta$ to $3\theta$ in 't' minutes. The temperature of the body after next 't' minutes is (Assume Newton's law of cooling and room temperature as $\theta$)
questions.solution:
According to Newton's law of cooling, the temperature $T$ at time $t$ is given by:

$T - T_s = (T_i - T_s)e^{-kt}$

where $T_s$ is the surrounding temperature and $T_i$ is the initial temperature.

For the first $t$ minutes, $T_i = 4\theta$, $T = 3\theta$, and $T_s = \theta$:

$3\theta - \theta = (4\theta - \theta)e^{-kt}$

$2\theta = 3\theta e^{-kt} \Rightarrow e^{-kt} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

For the next $t$ minutes, the initial temperature is $3\theta$. Let the final temperature be $T'$:

$T' - \theta = (3\theta - \theta)e^{-kt}$

$T' - \theta = 2\theta \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = \dfrac{4\theta}{3}$

$T' = \theta + \dfrac{4\theta}{3} = \dfrac{7\theta}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{7\theta}{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A monoatomic gas is stored in a thermally insulated container and the gas is suddenly compressed to $\left(\dfrac{1}{8}\right)^{th}$ of its initial volume. The ratio of final pressure to initial pressure is
questions.solution:
For a sudden compression in a thermally insulated container, the process is adiabatic.

The equation for an adiabatic process is $P V^{\gamma} = \text{constant}$.

For a monoatomic gas, $\gamma = \dfrac{5}{3}$.

Given $V_2 = \dfrac{V_1}{8}$.

$\dfrac{P_2}{P_1} = \left(\dfrac{V_1}{V_2}\right)^{\gamma}$

$\dfrac{P_2}{P_1} = (8)^{\dfrac{5}{3}} = (2^3)^{\dfrac{5}{3}} = 2^5 = 32$

The ratio of final pressure to initial pressure is $32:1$.

Answer: $32:1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In thermodynamic isobaric process
options: change in internal energy is zero
change in internal energy is not zero
questions.solution:
In an isobaric process, the pressure of the system remains constant ($P = \text{constant}$).

From the ideal gas equation $PV = nRT$, a change in state at constant pressure implies a change in both volume and temperature.

Since the temperature changes ($\Delta T \neq 0$), the change in internal energy $\Delta U = nC_v\Delta T$ is not zero.

Work done $W = P\Delta V$ is also not zero, and heat supplied $Q = nC_p\Delta T$ is not zero.

Answer: change in internal energy is not zero

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Light of wavelength $\lambda$ is incident on a single slit of width 'a' and the distance between slit and screen is D. In diffraction pattern, if slit width is equal to the width of the central maximum then D is equal to
questions.solution:
The linear width of the central maximum in a single slit diffraction pattern is given by $W = \dfrac{2\lambda D}{a}$.

Given that the width of the central maximum is equal to the slit width, we have $W = a$.

Equating the two expressions:

$\dfrac{2\lambda D}{a} = a$

$2\lambda D = a^2$

$D = \dfrac{a^2}{2\lambda}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When the distance of separation between the slit and screen is doubled, the angular separation between fringes in single slit diffraction pattern experiment
questions.solution:
The angular separation between fringes in a single slit diffraction pattern is given by $\Delta\theta = \dfrac{\lambda}{a}$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of light and $a$ is the width of the slit.

This expression is independent of the distance $D$ between the slit and the screen.

Therefore, when the distance of separation between the slit and screen is doubled, the angular separation between fringes remains the same.

Answer: remains same

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The fundamental frequency of sonometer wire is $50$ Hz for some length and tension. If the length is increased by $25\%$ by keeping the tension same, then the frequency change of second harmonic is
questions.solution:
The fundamental frequency of a sonometer wire is given by $f = \dfrac{1}{2L} \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$.

Since tension $T$ and mass per unit length $\mu$ are constant, the frequency is inversely proportional to the length, $f \propto \dfrac{1}{L}$.

The frequency of the second harmonic is $f_2 = 2f$, which also follows $f_2 \propto \dfrac{1}{L}$.

When the length is increased by $25\%$, the new length becomes $L' = L + 0.25L = 1.25L = \dfrac{5}{4}L$.

The new frequency of the second harmonic is $f_2' = f_2 \times \dfrac{L}{L'} = f_2 \times \dfrac{4}{5} = 0.8 f_2$.

The percentage change in the frequency of the second harmonic is $\dfrac{f_2' - f_2}{f_2} \times 100\% = \dfrac{0.8 f_2 - f_2}{f_2} \times 100\% = -20\%$.

Thus, the frequency of the second harmonic decreases by $20\%$.

Answer: decrease by $20\%$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A sonometer wire resonates with $4$ antinodes between the two bridges for a given tuning fork when $1$ kg mass is suspended from the wire. Using same fork, when mass M is suspended, the wire resonates producing $2$ antinodes between the two bridges. (Distance between the bridges as before) The value of M is
questions.solution:
The frequency of a sonometer wire is given by $f = \dfrac{p}{2L} \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$, where $p$ is the number of antinodes, $L$ is the length, $T$ is the tension, and $\mu$ is the linear mass density.

Since the frequency $f$, length $L$, and linear mass density $\mu$ are constant, we have $p \sqrt{T} = \text{constant}$.

Therefore, $p_1 \sqrt{T_1} = p_2 \sqrt{T_2}$.

Given $p_1 = 4$, $T_1 = 1 \times g$, $p_2 = 2$, and $T_2 = M \times g$.

Substituting the values, we get $4 \sqrt{1 \times g} = 2 \sqrt{M \times g}$.

Dividing by $2\sqrt{g}$, we get $2 = \sqrt{M}$.

Squaring both sides, $M = 4$ kg.

Answer: $4$ kg

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A Pipe open at one end has length $0.8$ m. At the open end of the tube a string $0.5$ m long is vibrating in its first overtone and resonates with fundamental frequency of pipe. If tension in the string is $50$ N, the mass of string is (Neglect end correction) (Speed of sound $= 320$ m/s)
questions.solution:
The fundamental frequency of a pipe open at one end (closed pipe) is given by $f_p = \dfrac{v}{4L_p}$.

Substituting the given values, $f_p = \dfrac{320}{4 \times 0.8} = 100$ Hz.

The string is vibrating in its first overtone, which corresponds to the second harmonic. The frequency of the string is $f_s = \dfrac{2}{2L_s} \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}} = \dfrac{1}{L_s} \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$.

Since the string resonates with the pipe, $f_s = f_p$.

$\dfrac{1}{0.5} \sqrt{\dfrac{50}{\mu}} = 100$

$2 \sqrt{\dfrac{50}{\mu}} = 100 \Rightarrow \sqrt{\dfrac{50}{\mu}} = 50$

Squaring both sides, we get $\dfrac{50}{\mu} = 2500 \Rightarrow \mu = \dfrac{50}{2500} = 0.02$ kg/m.

The mass of the string is $m = \mu L_s = 0.02 \times 0.5 = 0.01$ kg.

Converting to grams, $m = 10$ g.

Answer: $10$ gram

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wire is under tension of $2$ kg wt and a wave is travelling through it with some speed. Tension in the wire is so increased that the wave travels through it with thrice the original speed. The increase in tension is (in kg wt)
questions.solution:
The speed of a transverse wave in a stretched wire is given by $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$

where $T$ is the tension and $\mu$ is the linear mass density.

Since the speed is proportional to the square root of tension, we have $v \propto \sqrt{T}$

Given that the new speed is thrice the original speed, $v_2 = 3v_1$

$\sqrt{T_2} = 3\sqrt{T_1}$

$T_2 = 9T_1$

Given the initial tension $T_1 = 2$ kg wt, the new tension is $T_2 = 9 \times 2 = 18$ kg wt.

The increase in tension is $\Delta T = T_2 - T_1 = 18 - 2 = 16$ kg wt.

Answer: $16$
